MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L13·N578unmasked layer
This is a weak, diffuse neuron that fires on unstressed grammatical glue words mid-sentence — prepositions/connectives/possessives like "also", "at", "with", "to", "its" — and is suppressed on capitalized line-initial labels and rare word-initial subword fragments (e.g. "Action", "Mess"+ana, "b"+itters).

The neuron fires on ordinary mid-sentence continuation tokens (function words, possessives, appositive nouns) inside grammatically flowing prose — e.g. "In **this** guide", "change **in** human judgment", "Denver **voters**", "Lederer**’s**", "on **Tuesday**" — while it is strongly suppressed at breaks in headline/title-style fragments (colons, dashes, capitalized title words), so it appears to track "this sentence is continuing smoothly" rather than any single semantic topic.

L13·N13545unmasked layer
Fires on the whitespace token that immediately precedes a numeral in a coordinated list/pair of counts — typically the space after "and", "another", or a label colon in "10 X and 5 Y", "C: 0.828", "another 7 updates" (also the "and" itself in "winning ten and drawing one"); the same space-before-number position gives the strongest negative responses in other numeric-list contexts, so it is a positional numeral-separator detector rather than a semantic one.
